title: Beyond Visual Enhancement: Adaptive Multi-Context Steering to Mitigate LVLM Hallucinations
abstract: arXiv:2610.11907v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Hallucination remains a significant challenge in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). Existing training-free methods generally mitigate hallucinations through contrastive decoding or visual enhancement, often increasing the relative influence of visual evidence during generation. This raises a fundamental question: Can LVLMs dynamically regulate the contributions of different context sources to suppress hallucinations? In this work, we investigate and quantify how LVLMs coordinate multiple context sources during decoding and examine how this intrinsic behavior can guide hallucination mitigation. We find that LVLMs exhibit an intrinsic vision-attending tendency that can guide adaptive visual steering, while textual contexts can also contribute to hallucination mitigation. translated_title: 超越视觉增强：自适应多上下文引导以缓解大型视觉语言模型的幻觉
translated_abstract: 幻觉仍然是大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）面临的一项重大挑战。现有的无需训练的方法通常通过对比解码或视觉增强来缓解幻觉，这往往会在生成过程中增加视觉证据的相对影响力。这引出了一个根本性问题：LVLMs能否动态调节不同上下文来源的贡献以抑制幻觉？在这项工作中，我们研究并量化了LVLMs在解码过程中如何协调多个上下文来源，并考察了这种内在行为如何指导幻觉缓解。我们发现LVLMs表现出一种内在的视觉关注倾向，这种倾向可用于指导自适应的视觉引导，同时文本上下文也有助于缓解幻觉。受这些发现启发，我们提出了AIMS（自适应多源信息引导），一个轻量级的无需训练的框架，能够自适应地协调视觉、提示等上下文来源……
tldr: 提出了无需训练的AIMS框架，通过自适应协调视觉、文本等多种上下文来源的贡献来缓解大型视觉语言模型的幻觉问题，突破了传统单纯依赖视觉增强的局限。
